title: Orthogonality, Projections & Least Squares
interviewAnswer: Least squares can be understood as projecting the target vector onto the column space of the design matrix; the residual is orthogonal to that space at the optimum.
keyPoints: Rank deficiency makes solutions non-unique without additional choices.
QR/SVD are numerically preferable to explicit matrix inverse.
why: Orthogonality, Projections & Least Squares is a recurring foundation across data science and machine learning because it affects both theoretical correctness and practical system behavior.
deepDive: Least squares can be understood as projecting the target vector onto the column space of the design matrix; the residual is orthogonal to that space at the optimum. Rank deficiency makes solutions non-unique without additional choices. QR/SVD are numerically preferable to explicit matrix inverse. The interview-level skill is not merely recalling the definition: explain the assumptions, what diagnostic evidence you would inspect, and what alternative you would choose when those assumptions fail.
workedExample: Fit linear regression by projecting y onto the span of feature columns.
commonMistakes: Using the concept mechanically without checking assumptions or data semantics.
Reporting one metric/result without examining uncertainty, slices or failure modes.

production: In production, make assumptions explicit, validate on representative slices, compare with a simple baseline and monitor the signals that can drift.
